spans.s:
r. 10 cl. (गदति)
1 To speak articulately.
2 To be sick.
r. 10th cl. (गदयति)
To thunder.

m. (-दः)
1 Disease, sickness.
2 Speech, speaking.
2 GADA the younger brother of KṚṢṆA.
f. (-दा)
1 A mace, a club.
2 Trumpet flower, (Bignonia suave-olens.)
E.
गद to speak, &c. अच् aff.

mfn. (-त्नुः-त्नुः-त्नु)
1 Loquacious, talkative, talking much or idly.
2 Libidinous, lustful, desirous.
m. (-त्नुः)
A name of KANDARPA, the deity of love.
E.
गद to speak, Uṇādi affix इत्नुच्, and अय inserted.

n. (-ख्यं)
A kind of Costus, (C. speciosus): see कुष्ठ.

m. (always dual -दौ)
The two physicians of Svarga, the sons of AŚVINĪ by SŪRYA.
E.
गद disease in general, and अगद health.

m. (-जः)
A name of VIṢṆU or KṚṢṆA.
E.
गद, and अग्रज an elder brother.

m. (-रः)
A name of KṚṢṆA.
E.
गदा a club, and धर who holds; KṚṢṆA or VIṢṆU is represented holding a mace in one of his hands.

m. (-भृत्)
1 A name of KṚṢṆ

A mace or club bearer.
3 One who fights with a mace.
E.
गदा a club, and भृत् who nourishes: see the preceding.

m. (-रः)
A cloud.
E.
गद sound, अम्बर the sky.

m. (-तिः)
A drug, a medicament.
E.
गद, and अराति an enemy.

n. (-ह्वं)
A kind of grass, (Costus speciosus): see कुष्ठ.
E.
गद disease, and आह्वा a name; named by many of the same terms as disease: see व्याधि, &c.; also गदाख्य, गदाह्वय, &c.

mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
Spoken, said.
E.
गद to speak, क्त aff.

mfn. (-वान्-वती-वत्)
Saying, speaking, having spoken.
E.
गद, and क्तततु aff.

m. (-दी)
1 A name of VIṢṆ

A mace bearer.
3 One armed with a club.
4 A sick man.
E.
गदा a mace, and इनि poss. aff.

m. (-दः)
Indistinct or convulsive utterance, as sobbing, &c.
E.
गद to speak, क्विप् affix, root repeated with अच्.

m. (-निः)
Low inarticulate expression of joy or grief.
E.
गद्गद inarticulate utterance, and ध्वनि sound.

n. (-दं)
Inarticulate speech. गद्गद, and पद a word.

f. (-बाक्)
Inarticulate or convulsive speech, interrupted by sobbing, &c.
E.
गद्गद, and वाच् speech.

mfn. (-द्यः-द्या-द्यं)
To be spoken or uttered.
n. (-द्यं)
Prose.
E.
गद to speak, affix यत्.

n. (-कं)
A weight either of sixty-four or forty-eight Rattis; also read गद्यालक.
